- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-1.0) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly, especially if recent price is falling.
- Overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days) are common; apply downward correction of 10-20% of overshoot magnitude.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5-15%.
- If sentiment flips from positive to negative within 3-5 days, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 5-10% in next 5 days.
- Forecasting horizon 30d is prone to lag; if true outcome is below 30d forecast by >5%, consider 10-15% downward adjustment for next 7 days.
- When sentiment history shows repeated “1.0” followed by “-1.0”, model tends to overcorrect; avoid sharp downward moves after positive sentiment peaks.
